get.description:
Collects a media job that outlived the synchronous request that started it. When a media call runs past the gateway's wait budget it answers 504 with a `job_id` in the error body; the work carries on server-side and is still billed, so this endpoint is the only way to retrieve a result that has already been paid for.

Despite the `/v1/images` path it serves EVERY durable media job — image, video, 3D, upscale, speech and transcription alike — because jobs are looked up by id and workspace with no modality check. A job id from another workspace is reported as not found.

Poll until `status` reaches a terminal value: `completed` or `failed`. `queued` and `processing` mean work is still outstanding. Polling itself is not billed and settles nothing — the job's credits are settled by the worker and appear as `credits_used` once it completes.

On `completed`, a `data[].url` over our own durable copy is signed per read and lives 900 seconds, so use it rather than store it. Artifacts can be evicted by the storage sweeper or deleted through `DELETE /v1/files/{fileId}`; when that has happened `artifacts_expired` is set and `data` is shorter than the job produced.

It is a BILLING dimension on per-megapixel models, which is why the ceiling exists: the cost is `megapixels × $/MP × max(1, steps ÷ the model's default steps)`, so asking for more steps than the default multiplies the price of the call rather than leaving it unchanged.

Only the Together path forwards it to a provider. On every other image source it still validates and still prices, but the image comes back rendered with the model's own step count.

Let the model rewrite the prompt before rendering. Read by the Alibaba/DashScope path only, which treats an absent value as `true`; every other image source ignores it.

It also SELECTS A PRICE on `z-image-turbo`, where prompt extension is the expensive mode: the credit hold and the settle look that model's rate up under `extend`, or under `noextend` when this is explicitly `false`. Sending `false` is how you ask for the cheaper rate.

200.description:
Without `stream` (the default) this is `application/json` — one result object, shown below.

With `stream: true` IN THE BODY it is `text/event-stream` instead: a sequence of `data: <json>\n\n` lines terminated by a literal `data: [DONE]`. OpenAPI 3.0 has no vocabulary for "repeat this, then terminate with a sentinel", so the `text/event-stream` schema below describes the JSON payload of a SINGLE `data:` line — never the whole body — which is the precedent `chat/completions` (PR #766) and `music/generations` (#819) set.

One schema rather than music’s three-member `oneOf`, because there is one frame shape here: `status` is a STATE, not a discriminant. Frames run `queued` → `processing` → a terminal `completed` or `failed`, and the images arrive on the `completed` frame’s `data` — there is no separate result frame after it.

Two things the stream does NOT carry, both of which the JSON body does. `credits_used`: settlement runs AFTER the stream is closed, so a streamed generation never reports what it cost in band — the `x-request-id` response header is what ties the call to its usage record. And `file_id` on an artifact: registering images as durable files belongs to the media-job path, which a streaming request never takes.

quality.description:
Output quality. Checked against the chosen model's own input schema — refused with 400 when that schema is the provider's own and the value is not in it, snapped for a synthesized schema, and dropped for a model that declares no `quality` at all. OpenAI's `standard`/`hd` and GPT Image's `low`/`medium`/`high`/`auto` are two such sets among many; read the one that applies from `GET /v1/models`.

What it does on THIS endpoint is select a price, not a rendering: the credit hold and the settle look the image price up by quality, and no edit path forwards the value to a provider (OpenAI's edit is a multipart form that omits it; the FAL and Replicate input mappers exclude it). post.description:
Synthesizes `input` into speech and streams the AUDIO BYTES back. **The success response is not JSON** — read it as a stream or a buffer. Only the error responses carry a JSON body.

BILLED, and text-to-speech models are normally priced per character, so cost tracks the length of `input` rather than the length of the audio. The credits actually deducted come back in the `x-credits-used` response header. The API key's rate limit, allowed-model list and budget are enforced before the provider is called.

`input` is capped at 4096 characters and `speed` at 0.25–4.0; either overrun is a 400 before anything is billed. `voice` is OPTIONAL — omit it and the routed provider supplies a default — and its accepted values are model-specific, so read them from `allowed_params` on the model's `GET /v1/models` entry.

One case breaks the "always audio" rule and a client must handle it: if synthesis outlives the gateway's wait budget, the response is a JSON error carrying a `job_id`. The job keeps running and is still billed, and the finished audio is then collected from `GET /v1/images/jobs/{id}` — which answers a signed download URL, not audio bytes.

Voice to use for synthesis. Accepted values are model-specific — see `allowed_params` on the model's `GET /v1/models` entry.

OPTIONAL. Omitting it is a supported call, not a degraded one, but WHICH voice you get is the routed provider's answer rather than one of ours: the OpenAI and Google paths substitute `alloy` (Google then maps that name onto one of its own voices), the xAI path substitutes `eve`, and the Alibaba, FAL and Replicate paths send no voice at all so the model applies its own default. Pass one when the voice matters.

Sending one is not a guarantee either. On FAL and Replicate the value is forwarded only when the chosen model's own input schema declares a voice field that takes a NAME, and only when the value is a member of that field's enum where it has one — anything else is dropped silently so the model falls back to its default, rather than failing the request on a name that model has never heard of.

Without `?stream=true` (the default) this is `application/json` — one result object, shown below. Audio is uploaded to private storage and returned as a signed `url` (7-day expiry); if the storage upload fails, the response falls back to inline `b64_audio`.

The `error` frame is a real failure delivered as a frame — once SSE headers are flushed the gateway cannot answer with an HTTP status, so the response is still a 200 that ends in `[DONE]` — and `credits_used` appears ONLY on the `completed` frame, so a client that ignores `type` sees a successful, empty, apparently free stream.

post.description:
Terminal events for a run are delivered to the workspace notification channels subscribed to the event type (configure them at settings/notifications); a workspace with no matching subscription gets the default owner email instead. There is no per-run webhook override — the removed `webhook_url` field never routed anything (#525). ORDERING: a run may send more than one terminal event — a run reaped as failed whose worker then finishes sends a second, corrected event. Terminal events are delivered by a retrying, multi-worker queue and may arrive out of order, so order them by payload, not by arrival: for a given metadata.runId, a terminal event carrying metadata.correctsPriorStatus SUPERSEDES any terminal event that does not, regardless of arrival order. Once you have applied a correction for a run, discard any later terminal event for that run lacking the field. Full payload contract: docs/guides/pipeline-run-webhooks.md

THIS SPENDS CREDITS. Every step settles against the workspace wallet as it dispatches; there is no pre-flight balance gate and no cap derived from `POST /v1/workflows/estimate`, which is a quote. A run that fails half way has still paid for the steps that ran — and does not have to pay for them twice: send its id as `resume_from_run_id` to continue it from the step that failed. To re-run part of a workflow that already ran — because a prompt, a model or a parameter changed — send `rerun_from_step_id` alongside it: that step and every step that reads its output run again, and nothing else is dispatched or billed.

THE RESPONSE DEPENDS ON `mode`, and the three shapes have nothing in common:
- `sync` (default) — the request is held open until the run reaches a terminal state, then returns the whole run. A run that FAILS still returns 201 with `status: "failed"`; only a refusal before the run starts is a 4xx. Note two differences from `GET /v1/workflows/runs/{id}` on the same run: `input` is not echoed here, and `error.stepId` is present here and absent there.
- `async` — returns `{ id, status: "queued", createdAt }` immediately; poll `GET /v1/workflows/runs/{id}`.
- `stream` — returns `text/event-stream`, NOT JSON. Named SSE events: `pipeline.started`, `step.started`, `step.delta`, `step.completed`, `step.failed`, `step.skipped`, `foreach.started`, `iteration.started`, `iteration.succeeded`, `iteration.failed`, `foreach.completed`, and one of `pipeline.completed` / `pipeline.failed`, followed by a final `data: [DONE]`. A `: ping` comment is written when nothing else has been sent for 15s. A `sub_pipeline` child's own events are not proxied into the parent stream.

Supply EXACTLY ONE of `definition` or `pipeline_id`. Running a stored workflow requires only VISIBILITY of it, not edit access — a read share is permission to run. Sending both is a 400 (`ambiguous_definition`), sending neither is a 400 (`missing_definition`).

parameters.description: Replay guard, scoped to the workspace and never expired: a second run with a key already seen returns the FIRST run instead of executing again, in every mode. In `stream` mode a completed run is replayed as a synthetic event sequence, and a run still in flight is a 409 (`idempotency_in_progress`). The value is stored in a 120-character column and is not length-checked before that, so keep keys short.

201.description: One of two JSON shapes, by `mode`: the completed run (`sync`), or the queued run's identity (`async`). With `mode: "stream"` the response is `text/event-stream` — a sequence of the named SSE events listed in the operation description above, matching NEITHER JSON schema below. OpenAPI 3.0 has no way to express a dozen distinctly-shaped named event types, so the `text/event-stream` entry is deliberately just `{type: "string"}`: an honest admission that this document cannot describe that body, not a claim that it is JSON or that it matches either schema below.

400.description: Refused before anything ran, so nothing was billed and no run row exists: both or neither of `definition`/`pipeline_id`; a definition the schema or validator refuses; run input that fails the workflow's declared `inputs`; or an `only_step_id` that names no step, is missing an upstream result, has no `pipeline_id`, or was sent with `mode: "async"`.

post.description: Takes no request body. Sets a cancellation flag the runner checks BETWEEN steps, closes any step row still `running`, removes the job from the queue if it has not started, and recurses into in-flight child runs. BEST-EFFORT, and what that costs: a step already dispatched runs to completion and is billed, and it may settle `succeeded` after the cancel — a cancelled run truthfully containing a succeeded step is not a bug. Nothing already settled is refunded. Idempotent: cancelling a run that has already ended is a no-op that echoes the status it already had, so a `succeeded` in the response means the run beat the cancel. ACCESS: whoever may START this run may stop it — the workflow it belongs to must be visible to this caller, the same rule `POST /v1/workflows/runs` applies to that workflow. Deliberately NOT the reads' rule below: a share of the RUN discloses that run's results and does not carry cancellation, so a caller who can read a run this way still gets a 404 here. A run of an inline definition, or of a workflow that has since been deleted, belongs to no workflow the rule could apply to, and the workspace scope of the key is the whole rule for it.

arguments.description: A fragment of the JSON-encoded arguments string. Concatenate across chunks (by `tool_calls[].index`) to reassemble the full arguments.

index.description: Position of this tool call among the calls in progress. Accumulate `function.arguments` fragments PER INDEX — more than one call can be in flight, and the index is the only thing that separates them. See `ChatToolCallDto`'s doc comment.

id.description: Tool call id. Present only on the chunk that starts the call.

type.description: Present only on the chunk that starts the call.

role.description: Present only on the first chunk of the response.

content.description: A fragment of assistant text. Concatenate across chunks to reassemble the full message.

refusal.description: A fragment of a model refusal, in place of `content`.

annotations.description: Web-search `url_citation` annotations (OpenAI-grounded chat only). Attached, non-empty, to the delta of the FINAL content chunk by `ResponsesEventTranslator` — see `ChatAnnotationDto`.

tool_calls.description: Present while the model is calling a tool. May carry SEVERAL calls, and one call's fragments arrive across chunks — group by `tool_calls[].index`, never by array position. See `ChatToolCallDto`'s doc comment.

finish_reason.description: `null` on every chunk but the last one for this choice.

cached_tokens.description: Subset of `prompt_tokens` served from cache, billed at a reduced rate.

cache_write_tokens.description: Subset of `prompt_tokens` newly written to cache (default/5-minute TTL). OpenAI's own field, GPT-5.6 families onward.

cache_write_1h_tokens.description: Subset of `prompt_tokens` written to cache at Anthropic's 1-hour TTL — infery's own extension to the OpenAI-shaped block.

audio_tokens.description: Subset of `prompt_tokens` that was audio input. Forwarded verbatim from upstream on audio-capable models — never set by gateway code.

reasoning_tokens.description: Subset of `completion_tokens` spent on hidden reasoning (o-series/thinking models).

audio_tokens.description: Subset of `completion_tokens` that was audio output. Forwarded verbatim from upstream on audio-capable models — never set by gateway code.

prompt_tokens_details.description: Omitted entirely when nothing was cached, so a non-caching stream is byte-wise unchanged from before caching support existed.

title.description: Source title as the provider reported it. Empty string when the provider gave none.

provider.description: Which web-search provider served the grounding.

searches.description: How many searches were performed — what `web_search_credits` was charged for.

citations.description: Sources the answer was grounded in.

created.description: Unix timestamp. Absent on the final chunk of the generic streaming path (the one carrying `credits_used`) — see class doc comment.

model.description: Absent on the final chunk of the generic streaming path (the one carrying `credits_used`) — see class doc comment.

choices.description: Empty on the usage-only and final `credits_used` chunks; one entry otherwise (the gateway is single-choice throughout).

usage.description: Present on the usage chunk(s) near the end of the stream — token counts for the whole request. On the FINAL chunk (empty `choices`), accompanied by `credits_used`.

credits_used.description: Credits deducted from the workspace balance for this request. Set only on the LAST chunk before `data: [DONE]`, alongside `usage` and an empty `choices` array — added in `chat.controller.ts`'s streaming handler once the credit hold is settled.

web_search_credits.description: Credits charged for the grounded web search this request performed, SEPARATE from `credits_used`, which covers the model call. Present only when a web-search provider actually ran, on the same final chunk as `credits_used`. Undeclared until now, so a client generated from this document could not see half of what a grounded request cost.

infery_web_search.description: What the grounded search actually did, on the final chunk. Present only when a web-search provider ran. The same object appears on the non-streaming response body.

description.description: Description of what the function does, used by the model to decide when to call it.
description.example: Get the current weather for a location.

parameters.description: JSON Schema describing the function's parameters.

name.description: Name of the function tool to force.

url.description: Either an `http(s):` URL or a `data:<mime>;base64,<data>` data URI.

data.description: Base64-encoded file data. Alternative to `file_id` and `url` — see the class description.

file_id.description: Id of a file previously uploaded via `POST /v1/files`. Alternative to `data` and `url` — see the class description. May also be given as the shorthand `file_id` directly on the content part.

url.description: Source URL for the file content. Alternative to `data` and `file_id` — see the class description. Passed through as-is to the Anthropic and Google provider paths, which accept a file by URL natively.

file_id.description: Shorthand for `file.file_id` — the controller reads whichever is present (`file.file_id ?? file_id` at the top level). A `file_id` refers to a file from `POST /v1/files` and is resolved server-side into inline base64 (`file.data`/`file.mime_type`) before the provider sees it.

content.description: Message content: a plain string, or an array of content parts for multimodal input (text, `image_url`, `input_audio`, `file`).

tool_call_id.description: Id of the tool call this message answers. Present on a `role: "tool"` result message, echoing `id` from the assistant's `tool_calls` entry it responds to.

tool_calls.description: Tool calls made by the model. Present on an `assistant` message that called tools.

provider.description: Which search backend runs the query. `auto` (the default) derives it from the model family — `gpt-*`/`o*` → `openai`, `gemini*` → `gemini`, `claude*` → `anthropic` — and refuses with 400 `web_search_provider_required` for any other model, so a non-OpenAI/Google/Anthropic model must name a provider explicitly. `brave` is the decoupled path: the search runs first and its results are prepended to the conversation as a system message, and it is BILLED SEPARATELY from the completion (`web_search_credits` in the response). The other three are grounded natively by the upstream provider.

max_results.description: How many results to retrieve. Honoured on the `brave` path; the native grounded providers decide their own result count.

allowed_domains.description: Restrict results to these domains. Forwarded to Anthropic's native tool and honoured by the `brave` path; the OpenAI and Gemini grounded tools take no domain filter, so it is ignored there.

blocked_domains.description: Exclude these domains from results. Same reach as `allowed_domains`.

answer.description: Ask the search backend for a synthesised answer alongside the raw results, where it offers one.

model.description: Search-backend-specific model override. Distinct from the top-level `model`, which is the chat model that consumes the results.

seed.description: Seed for deterministic output (OpenAI, Google Gemini)

tools.description: Tool definitions available to the model. The gateway translates ONLY entries shaped `{type:"function", function:{name, description?, parameters?}}` into each provider's native tool-calling form; any other entry is forwarded upstream byte-identical — provider-native tools (web search, grounding, …) already arrive in their own shape.

tool_choice.description: Controls whether/which tool the model must call: `"none"`, `"auto"`, `"required"`, or `{type:"function", function:{name}}` to force one specific function tool.

prompt_cache_key.description: Optional cache-routing key for providers that cache prompt prefixes per-server (xAI, OpenAI). Send the same value across turns of one conversation to improve cache hit rate. Mirrors OpenAI’s own parameter of the same name.

web_search.description:
Ground the completion in web search, without having to write a provider-native tool entry by hand. Sending this object is the opt-in; there is no boolean form and its absence means no search.

It is a SHORTHAND over `tools`, and the two reach the same place: the gateway resolves a backend from `web_search.provider` (or the model family) and, for the natively-grounded providers, injects the matching entry into `tools` before forwarding — then removes `web_search` itself, so the upstream provider never sees this key. Sending the provider-native tool entry in `tools` yourself is the equivalent long form and needs no `web_search`; send one or the other rather than both.

BILLED. The `brave` backend runs as a separate search charge reported as `web_search_credits` on the response, on top of the completion's own tokens; the natively-grounded backends bill through the upstream provider's own search pricing.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code. Branch on this rather than on `message`, which is prose and may be reworded.

param.description: Name of the request parameter that triggered the error. `null` when the error is not attributable to one field.

job_id.description:
Handle to work that is ALREADY RUNNING AND ALREADY BILLED, present on the few errors that carry one. When it is here, this is not a failure to retry — retrying pays twice. Collect the result from `GET /v1/images/jobs/{job_id}`, which serves every durable media job regardless of modality.

Two situations produce it. A media generation that outruns the gateway's wait answers `504` with `code: "job_timeout"` and keeps working. And `POST /v1/audio/speech` answers **500** with `code: "artifact_unreadable"` when the speech was generated and settled but could not be read back from storage — the audio exists and is paid for; only this response failed.

Declared here rather than per-endpoint because the rule is about the FIELD, not the status: if this is present, there is a paid-for result to collect. It was undeclared until now, so a client generated from this document could not see the one field that recovers money already spent.

error.description: The error envelope. Every non-2xx response from this API has this shape, so a client can parse failures without branching on the endpoint.

url.description: Where the artifact can be downloaded. Normally a signed URL over the durable copy in our own storage, minted afresh on every read and valid for 900 seconds — so it must be used, not stored. For artifacts that were never registered as files (video jobs, and jobs predating artifact registration) it is instead the provider-hosted URL recorded on the job, which expires roughly an hour after the job ran and cannot be reissued.

file_id.description: Identifier of the durable `ApiFile` this artifact was registered as, usable with `GET /v1/files/{fileId}` and `GET /v1/files/{fileId}/content`. Omitted (never null) when no file was registered for this artifact.

id.description: The job id — the same value that was handed back in the 504 body when a synchronous call gave up waiting.

status.description: Job state. `completed` and `failed` are TERMINAL — stop polling on either. `queued` and `processing` mean work is still outstanding; keep polling. The internal `submitting` claim-lock state is reported as `processing`, so those four values are the whole published set.

progress.description: Completion percentage, 0–100. Uses the provider-reported figure, rounded and clamped, when the provider supplies one; otherwise an estimate derived from the poll counter and capped at 95 while the job is still running. 100 once the job settles.

data.description: The produced artifacts. Present only when `status` is `completed`; absent for every other state. May be empty, or shorter than the job produced — see `artifacts_expired`.

payload.description: The non-file deliverable, for the modalities that have one — a transcription's `text` and `language`, music's `duration_seconds`. Present only when `status` is `completed` and the job recorded one; omitted entirely for the file-delivering modalities. The keys belong to the modality and are not modelled here.

credits_used.description: Credits settled for the job (1 credit = $0.01). Present only when `status` is `completed`. May be fractional.

artifacts_expired.description: Present, and always `true`, when at least one artifact this job produced can no longer be handed back — the stored file was evicted by the storage sweeper, deleted via `DELETE /v1/files/{fileId}`, or was never reachable by any channel. `data` is then shorter than the job produced. Absent means nothing is known to be missing.

error.description: The failure reason recorded on the job. Present whenever the job recorded one — normally alongside `status: "failed"`.

url.description: Provider-hosted download URL for this image. Ephemeral — roughly an hour — so copy the bytes rather than storing the URL.

b64_json.description: Inline base64-encoded image bytes. Present when `response_format=b64_json` was asked for, and always for the GPT Image models, which return bytes exclusively.

revised_prompt.description: The prompt as the model rewrote it (DALL·E 3; the Google models echo the request prompt here).

status.description: The provider's normalised state. Read it before anything else: `failed` is a real failure delivered as a FRAME — once the SSE headers are flushed the gateway cannot answer with an HTTP status, so the response is still a 200 that ends in `data: [DONE]`, and a client that ignores `status` sees a successful, empty, apparently free stream.

progress.description: Percentage, 0-100. Advisory: providers step it in fixed jumps rather than reporting real progress.

data.description: The generated images. Sent ONLY on the `completed` frame — this is the deliverable, and it is the last frame before `data: [DONE]`. No `file_id` here, unlike the JSON 200: registering artifacts as durable files belongs to the media-job path, and a streaming request never takes it (`images.controller.ts` keeps `stream: true` on the inline path because the job facade has no channel for progress events).

error.description: Failure message. Present only on a `failed` frame.

url.description: Provider-hosted download URL for this image. Ephemeral — these expire in roughly an hour, so download or copy the bytes promptly rather than storing the URL. Absent when the model answered with inline bytes instead (`b64_json`), which is why this is OPTIONAL here while `MediaArtifactDto.url` is required: `ImageResult` (`providers/image-types.ts`) declares all of `url`/`b64_json`/`revised_prompt` optional, and each direct provider populates whichever the request asked for.

b64_json.description: Inline base64-encoded image bytes. Present when `response_format=b64_json` was asked for, and always for the GPT Image models, which return bytes exclusively.

revised_prompt.description: The prompt as the model rewrote it (DALL·E 3; the Google models echo the request prompt here).

file_id.description: Identifier of the durable `ApiFile` this image was registered as, usable with `GET /v1/files/{fileId}` and `GET /v1/files/{fileId}/content`. Only produced on the media-job path, and omitted (never null) for an artifact whose registration failed — registration is bookkeeping and never blocks or reshapes the deliverable. Registered bytes count towards the workspace storage quota.

created.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of when the result was produced.

data.description: One entry per produced image, in the order the provider returned them.

credits_used.description: Credits actually settled for this request (1 credit = $0.01). May be fractional.

url.description: Signed URL to the generated audio (private, 7-day expiry). The primary field — the same offloaded track the non-streaming 200 carries, because the `completed` frame is built from the same `offloadTrackToGcs` pass.

b64_audio.description: Base64-encoded audio bytes. Present only when the GCS upload failed, or on a provider that returns inline bytes exclusively.

content_type.description: MIME type of the audio (`audio/mpeg` for Lyria; varies per provider).

duration_seconds.description: Parsed duration of the generated track, in seconds.

type.description: Discriminant. Repeats while the track renders; a stream can carry any number of these, including none.

status.description: The provider's normalised job state. `completed`/`failed` can appear HERE, on a progress frame, before the terminal `completed`/`error` frame arrives — this is the job's state, not the stream's.

provider_status.description: The provider's own untranslated status string.

message.description: Human-readable progress note, when the provider supplies one.

error.description: A provider-reported error on a STILL-OPEN stream — the generation may still succeed. The terminal failure is the `error` frame, whose `error` is an object rather than this string.

data.description: Tracks a provider reported early. Rarely populated; the deliverable arrives on the `completed` frame.

type.description: Discriminant. Terminal success — exactly one of this or `error` arrives, immediately before `data: [DONE]`.

created.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of when the generation completed.

credits_used.description: Credits settled for this request (1 credit = $0.01). THE ONLY PLACE a streamed generation's cost appears — a stream has no JSON body to carry it and no `x-request-id`-bearing 200 envelope, so a client that ignores this frame never learns what it paid.

model.description: Slug of the model that actually ran, which fallback may make different from the one requested.

fallback_from.description: Slug originally requested, present only when fallback moved the request off it.

status.description: HTTP status this would have been, had the headers not already been flushed.

type.description: Discriminant. Terminal failure. Once SSE headers are sent the gateway cannot answer with an HTTP status, so a real failure arrives as a FRAME and the stream still ends with `data: [DONE]` and a 200 — a client that ignores `type` sees a successful, empty stream.

model.description: Slug of the 3D model to run, as listed by `GET /v1/models`. Must be an `object_3d`-modality model served by FAL; anything else is rejected with 400.

prompt.description: Text prompt for text-to-3D. Either `prompt` (non-blank) or `image_url` must be supplied; both may be. Rejected above 5000 characters.

image_url.description: Reference image for image-to-3D, as a URL. Forwarded onto the model's own image input field when it declares one, and dropped otherwise. Either `prompt` or `image_url` must be supplied.

mesh_url.description: An existing mesh to transform, as a URL. This is what the 3D-to-3D models take — rigging, remesh, retexture, segment. Forwarded onto whichever field the model's own schema declares for it (`mesh_url` on hi3d and tripo, `model_url` on meshy). A model that transforms a mesh REQUIRES this and is refused without it; a model that generates one refuses it.

url.description: Provider-hosted download URL for the generated mesh. This is the upstream (FAL) CDN link and expires in roughly an hour — download or copy the bytes promptly rather than storing the URL.

content_type.description: MIME type the provider reported for the mesh file (the deliverable is usually a `.glb`). Present only when the provider supplied one; on the synchronous path the same value applies to every entry.

file_id.description: Identifier of the durable `ApiFile` this mesh was registered as, usable with `GET /v1/files/{fileId}` and `GET /v1/files/{fileId}/content`. Only produced on the media-job path, and omitted (never null) for an artifact whose registration failed. Registered bytes count towards the workspace storage quota.

created.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of when the result was produced.

data.description: One entry per produced mesh, in the order the provider returned them.

credits_used.description: Credits actually settled for this request (1 credit = $0.01). Settled against measured compute for per_second models, clamped to the amount reserved before the call, so it is never larger than the hold. May be fractional.

model.description: Slug of the upscale model to run, as listed by `GET /v1/models`. Must be an `upscale`-modality model that accepts an image input and is served by FAL; anything else is rejected with 400.

image_url.description: Source image to upscale, as a URL or a data URI. Required.

url.description: Provider-hosted download URL for this artifact. These are the upstream (FAL) CDN links and expire in roughly an hour — download or copy the bytes promptly rather than storing the URL.

file_id.description: Identifier of the durable `ApiFile` this artifact was registered as, usable with `GET /v1/files/{fileId}` and `GET /v1/files/{fileId}/content`. Only produced on the media-job path, and omitted (never null) for an artifact whose registration failed — registration is bookkeeping and never blocks or reshapes `url`. Registered bytes count towards the workspace storage quota.

created.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of when the result was produced.

data.description: One entry per produced artifact, in the order the provider returned them.

credits_used.description: Credits actually settled for this request (1 credit = $0.01). Settled against measured compute for per_second models, clamped to the amount reserved before the call, so it is never larger than the hold. May be fractional.

model.description: Slug of the upscale model to run, as listed by `GET /v1/models`. Must be an `upscale`-modality model that accepts a video input and is served by FAL; an image upscaler is rejected with 400 and directed to `POST /v1/images/upscale`.

video_url.description: Source video to upscale, as a URL or a data URI. Required.

scale.description: Upscale factor. Forwarded onto whichever of the model's own input fields is named `scale`, `upscale_factor` or `upscaling_factor`; silently ignored by a model that declares none of them. Omit to use the model's own default.

size.description: Image size, e.g. "1024x1024" or a provider label ("1K").

quality.description: Image quality (DALL-E standard|hd, GPT Image low|medium|high|auto).

imageInputCount.description: Number of source images (per_image edit mode). 1 for edits, 0 for generate.

maxOutputTokens.description: Upper bound of output tokens for text models.

title.description: Human-readable label for this worked example.

params.description: A `params` object valid against this capability's `params_schema`.

currency.description: Always `credits` — the unit customers spend from their wallet. 1 credit = $0.01.

unit.description: Billing unit. `per_token` surfaces the `*_per_million` fields below; every other unit surfaces exactly one `{unit}_price` field.

input_per_million.description: Credits per 1M input tokens. Present when `unit` is `per_token`.

output_per_million.description: Credits per 1M output tokens. Present when `unit` is `per_token`.

audio_input_per_million.description: Credits per 1M audio input tokens. Present when `unit` is `per_token`.

audio_output_per_million.description: Credits per 1M audio output tokens. Present when `unit` is `per_token`.

image_input_per_million.description: Credits per 1M image input tokens. Present when `unit` is `per_token`.

image_output_per_million.description: Credits per 1M image output tokens. Present when `unit` is `per_token`.

cached_input_per_million.description: Credits per 1M input tokens served FROM the prompt cache — cheaper than the input rate. Omitted when no cached rate is published, in which case the full input rate applies.

cache_write_per_million.description: Credits per 1M tokens written to the prompt cache at the default (5-minute) TTL — DEARER than the input rate. Omitted when no write rate is published.

cache_write_1h_per_million.description: Credits per 1M tokens written to the prompt cache at the 1-hour TTL — dearer again. Omitted when no 1-hour rate is published.

request_price.description: Credits per request. Present when `unit` is `per_request`.

image_price.description: Credits per image. Present when `unit` is `per_image`.

second_price.description: Credits per second of compute. Present when `unit` is `per_second`.

minute_price.description: Credits per minute. Present when `unit` is `per_minute`.

character_price.description: Credits per character. Present when `unit` is `per_character`.

operation_price.description: Credits per operation. Present when `unit` is `per_operation`.

megapixel_price.description: Credits per megapixel. Present when `unit` is `per_megapixel`.

id.description: Capability identifier, `<category>.<operation>`. This is the value to send as `type` on a workflow step and as the `:id` path parameter of `POST /v1/capabilities/{id}/run`.

description.description: One-line summary of what the capability does.

long_description.description: Long-form Markdown documentation for this capability. Present only for the capabilities that ship a documentation file.

input_modality.description: The modality (or modalities) this capability consumes. A single string for most capabilities; an array when it takes more than one kind of input.

composite.description: Present, and always `true`, for the multi-operation capabilities (`image.pipeline`, `audio.pipeline`, `video.pipeline`) whose `params` chain a list of operations in one call. Absent for single-operation capabilities.

params_schema.description: JSON Schema (draft-07) for this capability's `params` object, generated from its Zod declaration. Two caveats a client must know: cross-field rules declared as Zod refinements are DROPPED by the conversion and do not appear here (the "one of width/height required" style of constraint is enforced at run time regardless), and the document may carry `x-infery-unit` (what a numeric parameter is measured in), `x-infery-enum-labels` (a display name per enum value) and `x-infery-value-sources` (keys that are alternative spellings of one value) — vendor extensions every JSON Schema validator ignores by specification.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema (draft-07) for this capability's `input` object, generated from its Zod declaration. The same two caveats as `params_schema` apply.

sample_input.description: An `input` object valid against `input_schema`, for the capabilities that declare one.

examples.description: Worked `params` examples, for the capabilities that declare any.

pricing.description: Retail price for running this capability. Absent when the capability has no active catalogue price — which means the price is unknown, not that the capability is free.

data.description: Every capability in the taxonomy, grouped by category in the order video, audio, image, document, archive, web, code.

definition.description: Inline workflow definition (mutually exclusive with pipeline_id)

pipeline_id.description: Stored workflow UUID (mutually exclusive with definition)

input.description: Optional initial input — used for ${input.X} resolution where possible

step_id.description: The step id from the definition.

type.description: Estimate row kind. NOT identical to the definition's `step.type`: every capability step — `transform`, `code`, `web.search`, `image.resize`, … — comes back as one `capability` row carrying its runtime type in `capability_id`.

min_credits.description: Low end of the quote for this step, in credits. Floored to 0 for any step carrying a `condition`, because the step may not run at all. Does not always reconcile against a nested breakdown — see `body_steps`.

max_credits.description: High end of the quote for this step, in credits. For a `foreach` row this is already multiplied by the iteration count. `max_credits === min_credits` does NOT mean the figure is certain — read `note`.

note.description:
Ambiguity / fallback marker. An OPEN string, not a closed enum — treat an unrecognised value as "unknown, do not assume free". The values emitted today, and what each means:

- `unknown_model` — the model slug resolved to nothing. COULD NOT BE PRICED: the 0 is an absence of an answer, not a free step.
- `no_price_configured` — a capability step with no priced row. COULD NOT BE PRICED, not free.
- `sub_pipeline_not_found` — the child workflow does not exist, or is in another workspace. COULD NOT BE PRICED.
- `sub_pipeline_depth_exceeded` — nesting deeper than 3 levels; the rest of the chain is unpriced. COULD NOT BE PRICED.
- `sub_pipeline_estimate_unavailable` — the child lookup failed for a reason that is not a clean not-found (the database was unreachable). COULD NOT BE PRICED.
- `sub_pipeline_no_workspace` — a sub-workflow reached costing with no workspace to resolve it against. COULD NOT BE PRICED. Not reachable through this endpoint today, which always supplies one.
- `items_count_unknown` — a `foreach` whose `items` is a binding, so the iteration count is unknown until the run. PRICED, but the count is a ceiling.
- `params_unknown` — a media step with a binding parameter the pricer reads (`n`, `duration`, `size`, `resolution`, `quality`, `steps`, TTS `characters`), and every transcription step. PRICED as a range — EXCEPT when `min_credits === max_credits`, which marks a step that is genuinely UNDER-quoted by an amount the estimator cannot state.

The six marked COULD NOT BE PRICED all report 0 credits. A client that renders them as "free" is wrong; render them as unknown.

model.description: Model slug being priced. Present for `model` and `media` rows.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens the quote was computed against, for a `model` row. Counted on the UNRESOLVED step — a binding that will carry a large upstream result downstream is priced as the literal binding text, so this understates such a step.

max_output_tokens.description: The `max_tokens` the quote assumed, for a `model` row.

capability_id.description: The capability being priced, for a `capability` row — the same string as the definition's `step.type` (`code.run.python`, `web.search`, `image.resize`, …).

branches.description: For a `parallel` row: one entry per step of every branch.

child_pipeline_id.description: For a `sub_pipeline` row: the child workflow, when it was found and recursed into.

child_pipeline_version.description: For a `sub_pipeline` row: the child version that was priced.

child_breakdown.description: For a `sub_pipeline` row: the child workflow's own breakdown. Absent when the child was not found, is cross-workspace, or exceeded the depth limit — the matching `note` says which.

max_iterations.description: For a `foreach` row: the iteration ceiling the quote used (the step's `max_iterations`, at most 100).

items_known.description: For a `foreach` row: whether `items` is an inline literal array (true) or a binding whose length is unknown before the run (false).

items_count.description: For a `foreach` row: the literal item count. Present only when `items_known` is true.

body_steps.description: For a `foreach` row: EVERY step of the loop body, in array order, each priced for ONE iteration. The row's own `max_credits` is this sum times the iteration count. `min_credits` deliberately does NOT reconcile against this array when `items` is a binding (min is 0 — the loop may run zero times) or when a body step is `condition`-gated.

inner_step.description: For a `foreach` row: literally `body_steps[0]`. Retained because it is the published shape and existing clients read it; it is a window onto the first body step, not the body. The row's credits are never derived from it.

min_credits.description: Sum of the steps' `min_credits`. The low end of the quote, not a floor on what a run will cost.

max_credits.description: Sum of the steps' `max_credits`. NOT a cap on billing: a run settles per step against actual usage, and any step whose row carries a "could not be priced" `note` contributed 0 to this total.

breakdown.description: Per-step rows, in definition order. Container steps carry their own nested breakdowns, so the array is a tree rather than a flat list.

name.description: Human-readable name, unique to no one — two workflows in a workspace may share it. Identity is the returned `id`.

description.description: Free text shown beside the workflow in the dashboard. Not interpreted, not passed to any step.

definition.description: The workflow document: its `steps`, their bindings, and the `inputs` it declares. Validated by `parsePipelineDef` at this boundary, so a malformed definition is a 400 here and is never stored. The step union is defined in Zod (`schemas/pipeline-definition.schema.ts`) rather than as a class, which is why this is published as a free-form object rather than a modelled schema — read that file for the authoritative shape.

id.description: Workflow UUID. Unchanged by an update.

version.description: The version this write left as latest. Always 1 from `POST`. From `PUT` it is the previous latest + 1 when the request carried a `definition`, and the UNCHANGED previous latest when it did not.

name.description: The workflow name after the write.

workspaceId.description: Owning workspace UUID — always the workspace the API key belongs to.

description.description: Author-supplied description. Max 2000 characters. Null when never set.
description.example: Summarise the week and render a PDF

latestVersion.description: Highest version number that exists for this workflow. `PUT` increments it only when the request carried a `definition`; a name/description-only update leaves it unchanged.

isActive.description: Column default. No code path in this repo ever writes it, so it is `true` on every row; do not read it as an enable/disable switch.

updatedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last `PUT` (name, description or definition).

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp. Always null on these responses: both reads filter on `deletedAt: null`, so a deleted workflow is a 404 rather than a row with a value here.

createdByUserId.description: User the workflow was created by, when the creating API key could be attributed to a workspace member. Null for a key whose creator was deleted or has left the workspace — such a key creates `workspace`-scoped workflows instead.

sharingScope.description: Who may see this workflow, before per-user grants. `private` = its creator (plus workspace owners/admins); `workspace` = every member; `users` = the members it was explicitly shared with. New workflows land on `private` unless the API key had no attributable creator.

sharePermission.description: What the sharing grant permits. Consulted only for the `workspace` and `users` scopes. `read` allows running the workflow — it means "you cannot change it", not "you cannot use it".

items.description: One page of workflows this caller may see, newest first by `createdAt`.

total.description: Total workflows matching the SAME visibility filter as `items` — not the workspace total. A workflow the caller cannot see is counted nowhere.

limit.description: Page size actually applied, after the server clamp to 100.

name.description: Input name. Referenced inside the definition as `${input.<name>}`.

type.description: Declared value type. `image`, `video`, `audio` and `file` are plain strings carrying either a URL or a workspace-scoped file id.

required.description: Whether a run must supply this input. ABSENT MEANS REQUIRED — the validator treats a missing `required` as `true`, it does not default to optional.

default.description: The value a run receives when it OMITS this input (`applyInputDefaults`). Part of the run contract: a caller that sends nothing gets this.

savedValue.description: The value the EDITOR last saved for this input, so a workflow reopens showing what its author typed. NOT a default — nothing on the run path reads it, and a `required` input may carry one.

label.description: Display label for editors. Not read by the engine.

description.description: Display help text for editors. Not read by the engine.

description.description: Author-supplied description. Max 2000 characters. Null when never set.

definition.description: The stored workflow definition for `version`, exactly as it was written. Unmodelled here: its shape is the Zod schema in `schemas/pipeline-definition.schema.ts` (`steps[]`, `output`, `retry`, `failure_mode`, `inputs[]`, `ui`), which this document does not publish. It is returned as stored — the schema `.default()` values are NOT filled in on this read.

version.description: The version this `definition` came from: the `version` query parameter when one was given, otherwise `latestVersion`.

inputs.description: The declared run inputs read out of `definition.inputs`. `[]` for a legacy definition that predates the input contract, and also `[]` — never an error — when a hand-edited row carries a non-array `inputs`.

name.description: New name. Omit to leave it unchanged — this is a partial update, not a replacement.

description.description: New description. Omit to leave it unchanged.

The workflow document: its `steps`, their bindings, and the `inputs` it declares. Validated by `parsePipelineDef` at this boundary, so a malformed definition is a 400 here and is never stored. The step union is defined in Zod (`schemas/pipeline-definition.schema.ts`) rather than as a class, which is why this is published as a free-form object rather than a modelled schema — read that file for the authoritative shape.

Supplying it creates a NEW VERSION rather than editing the current one — earlier versions stay readable by `version`.

deleted.description: Always `true` — the route either soft-deletes and returns this, or throws.

code.description: Machine-readable failure code, as raised by the step executor or by the engine.

message.description: Human-readable failure message. Empty string when the row recorded a code but no message.

stepId.description: The step that failed. Present on the response of a run that failed IN THIS REQUEST (`POST /v1/workflows/runs` in sync mode). ABSENT from `GET /v1/workflows/runs/{id}`: the run row stores only the code and message, so re-reading a failed run does not tell you which step failed — read `stepRuns[]` for that.

code.description: Machine-readable failure code, as raised by the step executor or by the engine.

message.description: Human-readable failure message. Empty string when the row recorded a code but no message.

id.description: The STEP id from the definition — not a database row id. Repeats across entries when the step was retried.

type.description: The step type from the definition (`model`, `media`, `http`, `foreach`, `parallel`, `sub_pipeline`, or a capability id such as `image.resize`).

status.description: `skipped` means the step did not execute — see `skippedReason`, and note its `output` is then `null` on purpose. `cancelled` is written by the cancel sweep over rows still `running`; a step may still settle `succeeded` after that, which is truthful rather than a race to fix.

output.description: Whatever the step produced — the shape is the step type's, not a common one: an object for a model step, an array for `foreach` (one element per iteration), a Record keyed by branch id for `parallel`. `null` for a step skipped by a false condition. Absent when the step produced nothing (a failure).

outputRef.description: Handle for the artifact this step wrote, for binding downstream as `${steps.<id>.outputRef}`. Currently a `gs://<bucket>/<object>` URI (historically `file_id://<id>`) — an INTERNAL reference, not a fetchable URL. Published only by media and capability steps that produce a file; absent for transcription, for `sub_pipeline`, and for the container steps.

error.description: Present only when this attempt failed.

skippedReason.description: Why the step was not executed on this run. `condition_false` — its `condition` evaluated false. `resumed_from_prior_attempt` — an async retry reused the output an earlier attempt recorded, OR (with `resume_from_run_id`) this run inherited the result the resumed run produced. `not_selected` — a one-step run (`only_step_id`) stood this step in with its last recorded output. READ IT ALONGSIDE `status`, not instead of it: a resumed run's inherited step is `succeeded` AND carries `resumed_from_prior_attempt`, which together mean "this result is part of this run, and this run did not produce it" — its `creditsUsed` is 0 because this run paid nothing for it.

childRunIds.description: Child `pipeline_runs` this step spawned — `foreach` iterations, or the single invocation of a `sub_pipeline`. Always present, `[]` when the step spawned none. Each id is readable through `GET /v1/workflows/runs/{id}`.

creditsUsed.description: Credits actually settled for this attempt. 0 for a skipped step, and for a step that failed before dispatch.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock duration of this attempt in milliseconds. 0 when the step never dispatched.

attempt.description: 1-based attempt counter for this step within the run.

status.description: Terminal statuses are `succeeded`, `failed` and `cancelled`. `queued`/`running` are only ever seen by reading a run that has not finished. `partial` exists in the enum and no writer in this repo produces it — do not build on it.

attempt.description: Current run-level attempt, 1-based. Only an `async` run can exceed 1; `sync` and `stream` runs never retry at the run level.

maxAttempts.description: Run-level attempts configured, from the definition's `retry.max_attempts` clamped to 1..5. 1 for `sync` and `stream` runs.

input.description: The input the run was given, AFTER declared defaults were applied. Returned by `GET /v1/workflows/runs/{id}` and by an idempotent replay; ABSENT from the response of a fresh sync run, which is built from the runner's result rather than the row. `{}` is a real answer (the workflow declares inputs and the caller sent none) — the field is omitted, never null, when there is nothing.

output.description: The run's output, resolved from the definition's `output` block against the steps' results. Absent for a run that failed or was cancelled before producing one.

error.description: Present only for a failed run. A cancelled run carries no error.

creditsUsed.description: Credits actually settled for this run, summed from the per-step settles. This is real money spent — it is NOT the estimate, and it is not capped by one: `POST /v1/workflows/estimate` is a quote, and the `credits_reserved` figure the run row carries is written but read by nothing.

stepRuns.description: One entry per step ATTEMPT. Ordered by step id then attempt on `GET /v1/workflows/runs/{id}` — LEXICOGRAPHIC, not execution order — while a fresh sync run returns them in the order the runner executed them. Reading a run that is still `running` returns the steps written so far, including ones still `running` themselves.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock duration of the run in milliseconds. 0 when the row never recorded one.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the run was created.

id.description: Run UUID. Poll it with `GET /v1/workflows/runs/{id}`; there is no other handle to the job.

status.description: Always `queued`, including on an idempotent replay — this response reports that the run EXISTS, not what it is doing now. A replay of a key whose run has already finished still says `queued`; read the run to learn its real status.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the run row was created.

pipeline_id.description: Reusable workflow id (provide either this OR definition)

pipeline_version.description: Specific version of pipeline_id (defaults to latest)

definition.description: Inline workflow definition (use instead of pipeline_id)

mode.description: Execution mode (default sync). When "stream" the response is text/event-stream.

only_step_id.description: Run ONLY this step, using the outputs its upstream steps recorded on earlier runs. Requires pipeline_id, and every step it reads must already have a succeeded result. Not available with mode=async.

resume_from_run_id.description: CONTINUE THIS FAILED RUN instead of starting over: the steps it recorded as succeeded are reused, and only the step that failed and everything downstream of it runs again. A reused step is not dispatched and not billed. Send `definition` (or `pipeline_id`) alongside to fix the step that failed — swap the model, change the params, replace the step; send neither and the run is resumed against the definition it originally executed. REFUSED, before anything is billed, when: the run did not fail (`resume_run_not_failed`); the edit changes a step that already produced a result, which is a new run rather than a resume (`resume_upstream_definition_changed`); `input` differs from the input that run used (`resume_input_changed`); a reused step's artifact has since been deleted (`resume_artifact_expired`); the run did not record which version of the workflow it executed and the workflow has been saved since (`resume_source_definition_unknown`); or with `mode: "async"` (`resume_async_unsupported`) or with `only_step_id` (`resume_with_only_step`). A step with no recorded result — including one whose result was lost — simply runs again.

rerun_from_step_id.description: RUN THIS STEP AND EVERYTHING THAT DEPENDS ON IT, reusing the results of the run named by `resume_from_run_id` — which may be in ANY finished state (succeeded, failed or cancelled), not only failed. The step runs, every step that transitively reads its output runs, and every other step is reused from that run: not dispatched, not billed. DEPENDENCY-BASED, NOT POSITIONAL: a step declared after it that does not read it (directly or through another step) could not have a different result, so it is neither re-run nor re-billed. Send an edited `definition` (or `pipeline_id`) alongside to change what the step does — unlike a bare resume, an edit to a step that already produced a result is NOT refused here: it widens the set that runs again to include that step and everything below it, and the credit hold covers the wider set. A STEP WITH NO RECORDED RESULT ALWAYS RUNS AGAIN, which on a CANCELLED run means work that was in flight when it stopped may have been charged already and is charged again. REFUSED, before anything is billed, when: sent without `resume_from_run_id` (`rerun_from_step_without_run`); the run has not finished (`rerun_run_not_finished`); no step of the definition has this id (`rerun_from_step_unknown`); or with `mode: "async"` (`rerun_async_unsupported`). `resume_input_changed`, `resume_artifact_expired` and `resume_source_definition_unknown` apply here too.

id.description: The run the cancel was addressed to.

status.description: `cancelled` when this call moved the run. For a run that was ALREADY terminal the call is a no-op and this echoes the status it already had — so a `succeeded` here means the run finished before the cancel reached it, not that cancelling succeeded.

step_id.description: Workflow step identifier — the step id from the definition, matching `stepRuns[].id` on the run.

status.description: Call outcome. `in_flight` is a call that was still open when this was read — or one whose process died before it could be closed, which is why an old `in_flight` row is not evidence of a live call.

input_tokens.description: Provider-reported input tokens for this call. Null whenever the provider reported none — which is the normal case for media steps, and always the case for transcription, whose byte count is deliberately NOT written here to keep this column in one unit.

output_tokens.description: Provider-reported output tokens for this call. Null on the same terms as `input_tokens`.

settled_credits.description: Credits actually settled for this call. Null while the call is `in_flight`, and for a failure that settled nothing. This is the per-call component of the run's `creditsUsed`.

error_message.description: Provider or engine failure message for a `failed` call. Null otherwise.

started_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the call was opened. Rows are returned oldest-first by this field.

completed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the call was closed. Null while `in_flight`.

data.description: The run's model and media calls, oldest first. `[]` is a normal answer — for a workflow whose steps call no model, and for any run older than the 7-day retention window.

slug.description: Stable identifier, and the path segment for the detail route. Max 120 characters.

description.description: Catalog description. Always a string — the column is NOT NULL.
description.example: Summarise a week of notes and render a PDF.

category.description: Catalog category, or null when the template is uncategorised. The `category` filter matches this exactly.

tags.description: Free-form tags. The `tag` filter matches a template whose array CONTAINS the given tag.

step_types_used.description: The step types the template's definition uses, denormalised at seed time for filtering and display.

thumbnail_url.description: Preview image URL, or null when the template has none.

items.description: One page of templates, oldest first. Hidden templates are excluded from the list entirely — they are only reachable by slug.

total.description: Total templates matching the filters, counted with the same `unavailable_since IS NULL` exclusion as `items`.

reason.description: Operator-supplied reason. Empty string when the row was hidden without one.
